---
title: "Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim"
dek: "Nvidia's board announced the change on November 12, 2026 and named Harvey C. Jones its first chair. The company gave no reason for the departure."
---

Nvidia said on November 12, 2026 that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer and member of the board, "effective immediately".[^1]
The Form 8-K filed with the announcement says the board accepted the resignation on November 11, 2026.[^2]
Huang founded Nvidia in 1993 and had led it as CEO ever since.[^3]

## Who runs Nvidia now

Colette Kress, chief financial officer since September 2013, becomes interim CEO and keeps the finance job "until a permanent successor has been named".[^1]
The board said it is starting a search and "will consider internal and external candidates".[^1]
The 8-K is already signed by Kress under her new title.[^2]

The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its "first-ever Chair of the Board".[^1]
Jones, 73, has been an Nvidia director since 1993 and is managing partner of Square Wave Ventures, a private family office.[^2]
In the release he said the board "has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team" and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap "to continue without interruption".[^1]

## What the announcement leaves out

The release gives no reason for the resignation and does not mention any investigation.[^1]
The context comes from earlier coverage.
On November 8, 2026, Huang told Nvidia staff by email that he had had an affair, and that the board had opened an independent investigation, CNBC reported.[^5]
CNBC, citing reports in The New York Times and the Financial Times, wrote that U.S. intelligence agencies had expressed concerns that the woman, who is affiliated with an Nvidia customer, had been passing information to Beijing.[^5]
<!-- add role="reviser" model="Claude Opus 5.5" -->
China's foreign ministry said on November 9, 2026 that the allegation was "unsubstantiated", NBC News reported.[^9]
Megaspeed, the Nvidia customer the woman was affiliated with, said on November 12, 2026 that it "takes its compliance obligations under U.S. export control laws extremely seriously", according to CNN.[^5][^8]
<!-- /add -->

Those are allegations, not findings.
The board said on November 8, 2026 that it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised".[^5]
<!-- add role="reviser" model="Claude Opus 5.5" -->
The same day, the board said it was "initiating an independent investigation", overseen by a committee of independent directors with outside counsel.[^6]
<!-- /add -->
TechCrunch reports that the resignation came "just a few days after" Huang admitted the affair, and Al Jazeera that he stepped down "following espionage and affair allegations"; Nvidia itself has not linked the two.[^3][^4]

<!-- add role="reviser" model="Claude Opus 5.5" -->
## The investigation and the board

On November 10, 2026, the independent directors said they had hired Joon H. Kim, a former acting U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct it.[^7]
CNN and Al Jazeera both report that the board met late on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, after reports that Huang had also had a relationship with an Nvidia executive; Al Jazeera attributes those reports to The New York Times.[^8][^4]
None of the Nvidia statements cited here addresses those reports.[^1][^6][^7]

## Congress was already asking questions

Three House Republican committee chairs wrote to Huang on November 4, 2026 asking for a closed-door briefing, CNN and CNBC reported; CNBC gave the requested date as November 18, 2026.[^8][^5]
CNN reported that House Foreign Affairs chairman Brian Mast said Huang tentatively agreed on November 11, 2026 to testify.[^8]

<!-- /add -->
## Markets and the AI supply chain

Nvidia shares were "down nearly 12%" in early trading on November 12, 2026, according to TechCrunch; Al Jazeera put the slide at "roughly 10 percent" and said the company's market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025.[^3][^4]

The stakes go beyond one company.
Nvidia supplies most of the chips that power advanced AI systems.[^4]
It is also an investor in the labs that buy them: TechCrunch counts $30 billion put into OpenAI and $10 billion into Anthropic.[^3]
The same report says Huang ran a flat organization with around 60 direct reports and that there was no heir apparent or succession plan.[^3]

The first test for the interim team is close.
Nvidia said it will report third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, "as previously scheduled".[^1]
